evidence: The controlling plan requires P-RMT-01. Its current A page and batch-46 manifest were inspected. The MP law and nested real finite-fourth edge interfaces match the uses recorded below; this interface check is not independent proof review or publication acceptance.
The current definition uses the (t-z)^-1 convention for Im z>0, exactly the resolvent and population-transform convention used in the theorem.
The current lemma supplies inversion and uniqueness for Borel probability measures under the same (t-z)^-1 convention; its statement and complete proof were inspected.

The real supplier assumes a nested top-left iid array, mean zero, unit variance, finite fourth moment, and p_n/n->gamma. Apply it separately to the real and imaginary parts after normalizing each nonzero variance; SVD converts its largest-eigenvalue bound to an operator-norm bound. The current body and owner Step-1 ready record were inspected.
The current definition gives the density and zero atom with aspect gamma=p/n and normalization 1/p, which is the covariance convention in the risk corollary.
The current complete proof supplies the MP probability law, its (t-z)^-1 transform, and the fixed-point/branch bounds used to compute the positive-spectrum inverse moment.

The current real iid finite-fourth MP theorem states almost-sure weak ESD convergence with p_n/n->gamma and AC. The risk corollary states these assumptions and AC explicitly; the theorem body and owner Step-1 ready record were inspected.

The current owner-ready supplier states the nested real iid finite-fourth model, p_n/n->gamma, eventual rectangular rank, and positive lower nonzero edge for gamma!=1. The risk corollary uses this only to obtain the stated positive gap and continuous cutoff; the supplier and its owner readiness record were inspected.
The explicit density, zero atom, and aspect-ratio normalization match the c=n/N isotropic specialization after mapping the p-dimensional Hastie covariance to X^*X/n.
The fixed-point transform identity identifies the isotropic deformed law with the explicitly defined Marchenko-Pastur probability law by uniqueness.
At gamma=1 the formula has a=0, no zero atom, and density proportional to x^-1/2 near zero; the page uses this limiting-law fact only.
The complete transform and probability-law proof fixes the convention used for the critical-aspect continuous resolvent cutoffs.
